chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd and Fadala ibn Ayub together, from Musa ibn Bakr, from al-Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'except for the weakened ones from the men, women and children.' He said: It is the one who is unable to disbelieve, so he disbelieves, and is not guided to the path of faith so that he believes. And the children, and whoever of the men and women is upon the intellect of children, the pen is raised from them.

key_terms.الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ: The weakened ones (those unable to bear the burden of duty)
key_terms.مَرْفُوعٌ عَنْهُمُ الْقَلَمُ: The pen is raised from them (exempt from accountability)

ai.seo_question: Who are considered the 'weakened' in Quran 4:98 according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Baqir’s (AS) clarification that 'al-mustad'afin' refers not merely to the physically weak, but to those lacking the cognitive capacity for conscious choice, such as children and adults with similar mental states. This definition underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the 'pen of accountability' (raf' al-qalam) is lifted from those unable to distinguish right from wrong, thereby exempting them from religious duties and sins.

en.basel-kadem: 4.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Hussain ibn Hasan bn Aban, from Hussain bin Sa’eed, from Nadr bin Suwayd, and Fadala bin Ayub, all of them, from Musa bin Bikr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, that he said:

I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «except for the weakened ones from the men, women and children» [4:98], so he said: It is the one who does not purposely disbelieve, so he disbelieves and is not guided to the path of faith by which he believes, and so are children. Those from men and women who possess the same (level of) intellect as children, the pen [1] is raised from them.
